releases.name: reeve 0.3.0
releases.body:
**The review skill now ships every upstream rule doc (7 → 64), not a hand-picked
subset.** The previous snapshot was pinned at `alibaba/open-code-review` v1.13.1
with 7 rubrics chosen by language. Re-checking today: upstream is at **v1.13.8**
(64 docs, 324,004 bytes) and our 7 files are byte-identical to that tag, as is
the `Category`/`Severity` enum file — so the snapshot was stable, but the
selection was not: it missed the **domain** rules (`github_workflows.md`,
`github_config.md`) that cover the 9 workflows and 4 `.github` configs in
reeve + ocrc, and `yaml.md` was only 86 bytes ("check key spelling").

- `skills/review/` now carries all 64 upstream rule docs as verbatim copies,
  plus `UPSTREAM.sha256` (per-file hash pinned to a commit, not a tag).
- New `skills/review/review-map.json`: extension → rule selection table
  (REEVE-authored; upstream's internal mapping was never copied). The table in
  `SKILL.md` is **generated** from it, not hand-maintained.
- New `scripts/check-review-map.mjs`: `--write` regenerates the table,
  `--check` fails when the table is stale, a rubric is unlisted, two rules claim
  the same glob, or the representative path cases resolve to the wrong file.
- `scripts/check-plugin-pack.mjs` now also asserts
  `provision.json`'s `enginePlugin.spec === <name>@<version>`, that the packed
  rubric set matches `UPSTREAM.sha256` byte-for-byte, that
  `skills/review/` has no subdirectories, and accepts `--pkg-dir` so negative
  tests run against a throwaway copy.
- New `.gitattributes` pins `plugin/skills/review/*.md` (and the hash manifest)
  to LF; without it a Windows checkout rewrites line endings and the sha256
  gate fails on every Windows CI leg.
- `provision.json`: version 0.3.0, `enginePlugin.spec` caught up from 0.2.8
  (it had drifted since 0.2.9), `enginePlugin.entry` corrected to the real
  unpack layout (`.../components/reeve/package`).
- Notices updated: `NOTICE.md` and the in-package `THIRD-PARTY.md` both list
  all 64 files; upstream verified to have no `NOTICE` file of its own.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.12
releases.body:
**Contract-only release.** Adds `pluginOptions` (`agents.hideBuiltins=false`)
to `provision.json` so ocrc-driven peer installs register the plugin as an
object entry carrying the option — 0.2.11 shipped the feature but left the
contract field out, so peers kept the plain-string entry and native agents
stayed hidden there. No code changes.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.11
releases.body:
**Native agents can stay visible; foreman gets a shape-based fast lane.**

- New plugin option `agents.hideBuiltins` (default `true`, current behavior):
  when `false`, the engine's native `build` / `plan` / `general` / `explore`
  agents keep their config visibility and appear in the composer picker.
  Direct small tasks can then run on the native single-agent path (1× token
  cost) while foreman keeps handling orchestrated ones — the manual mode
  switch that every mainstream coding agent converged on, backed by the
  multi-agent overhead data (Anthropic's research system reports ~15× token
  usage vs a chat) and the SWE-bench gold-patch distribution (median 1–2
  files touched).
- `agents/foreman.md` dispatch judgment rewritten from task **type** to task
  **shape**: three questions (parallelizable subtasks? needs a boundary-locking
  doc? needs independent review?). All "no" → fast lane: one-sentence task
  straight to `executor`, personal verification, **no** planner/critic/reviewer;
  any "yes" → full pipeline. The old dispatch-gate ceremony (written
  justification required to skip planning) is retired — it made the 1–2-file
  majority of real work pay the orchestration tax by default. The ≤3-file
  hint is a calibration default, to be revisited against real dispatch
  ledger data, not a law.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.10
releases.body:
**Bare model names route to the pool instead of the paid default chain.** The
engine addresses models by bare id (`glm-5.3-flash-free`, no `provider/`
prefix) whenever its provider baseURL is overridden — and GATE's bare-name
fallthrough sent those requests to `default_chain`, silently serving them from
a **paid** candidate (observed live 2026-10-27: `glm-5.3-flash-free` landed on
zhipu). Now a bare name that matches a discovered free-pool model is routed as
an explicit direct (passthrough) target. Chain names and `chain_for_model`
keep their precedence; unknown bare names still fall to the default chain.

**Free-pool ordering matches reality.** `prefer` now leads with the two
openrouter candidates that actually hold quota through GATE (`nvidia/
nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` 1M-context vision, `dots-studio/dots-3-note-
preview:free`), with the zen pair (`glm-5.3-flash-free`, `mimo-v2.6-flash-
free`) following; `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` is denied by default —
it returned 429 on every attempt observed, including on days when its zen
siblings served 87% of traffic.

Diagnostic note from the same investigation: synthetic probes against
`opencode.ai/zen/v1` always answer 429 with `FreeUsageLimitError` regardless
of credentials or headers — that endpoint is not the one GATE uses
(`opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1`). Never judge pool health from probes;
judge from real-traffic ledger rows.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.9
releases.body:
**First-byte failover for streaming.** Live incident on 2026-10-26: zhipuai
answered `HTTP 200`, opened the SSE stream, then went silent — zero bytes for
~45s and counting. The 0.2.8 stream guard can only cool the model *after*
`finish`: response headers are already committed, so the turn is unsavable and
every concurrent subagent dies with it. The streaming branch is now a
**single-consumer pump** (one `for await` is the only reader — the previous
attempt at this deadlocked by mixing `pipe` with manual reads, and was
reverted):

- **Headers are not committed until the first byte arrives.** Before that
  point the chain can still move: a stalled or reset upstream is recorded as
  `error/stalled` (or `stream error`) in the ledger, cooled in the session and
  free-lane accounts, and the next candidate serves the request.
- **Real timers on silence, never on total duration.** `stream_first_byte_ms`
  (default 45s) guards the wait for the first byte; after that the window
  widens to `stream_idle_ms` (default 120s). A reasoning model that keeps
  producing is never touched — only silence is. A timer firing mid-stream
  aborts the upstream and truncates the response (headers are already out;
  nothing else is possible), recording exactly one failure — the `finish`
  empty-probe yields via the settled flag, so accounts are never
  double-booked. Client disconnects before the first byte clean up silently
  and are **not** charged to the provider.
- Two latent 0.2.8 defects fixed en route: the `pipe` never forwarded upstream
  errors (a stream reset before the first chunk left the client hanging — now
  it fails over), and the probe decoded chunks with `chunk.toString('utf8')`,
  which degrades to comma-separated decimal garbage on runtimes where
  `Readable.fromWeb` yields bare `Uint8Array` (every real stream would have
  been judged empty); decoding now goes through `TextDecoder`.
- Policy keys: `stream_first_byte_ms` / `stream_idle_ms` (exposed in
  `/gate/version` and the snapshot); the never-wired `first_prompt_watchdog_ms`
  default was removed.
